issue_context.title: Constructing DataFrames using range fails
issue_context.body:
Working on removing ``compat.lrange``, I've discovered that 1-dim lists, iterators and generators work as expected:

```python
>>> pd.DataFrame(list(range(3)))  # ok
   0
0  0
1  1
2  2
>>> pd.DataFrame(iter(range(3)))  # ok
   0
0  0
1  1
2  2
>>> pd.DataFrame((i for i in range(3))  # ok
   0
0  0
1  1
2  2
```

while constructing with a plain ``range`` does not work:

```python
>>> pd.DataFrame(range(3))  # not ok
AttributeError: 'range' object has no attribute 'ndim'
```

Fix upcoming.

review_comments: I would reference the issue as a comment above this line as well.
Oh, this is just an existing test that has been moved. It already passed before this PR.

A plain ``range`` isn't a iterator, so this fixes up the nomenclature.

The range case is now placed in ``test_constructor_list_of_ranges``, which is clearer.
